title: Crossings

rows.text: Crossings
12 draft packages. Images have no embedded text; wording listed as an overlay is rendered separately.
CROSS-01-A · Both Sides of the Laminate

The crossing supervisor admires Congress and Biden imposing a rail agreement in 2022. He offers you the same negotiation: a laminated sheet bolted to the counter. The bolts appear to represent your side.
Passage → You’re waved through. The supervisor congratulates both sides of the sheet on a successful negotiation.
Diversion → You take the diversion. The consultation ends with you consulting a map.
Permit receipt → Your permit settles it. He has finally met a document he didn’t write. One Receipt is used.
Permit tag → Your permit settles it. He has finally met a document he didn’t write. Your permit tag remains available.
Bribe success → Your payment secures passage. The negotiating table turns out to have a cash drawer.
Bribe failure → He keeps the money and refuses passage. Your position has been considered, then folded into his wallet.
Refused passage → He refuses passage; you take the detour. He records unanimous agreement among the bolts.

Scene: The current van occupants face a crossing supervisor at a roadside counter with a blank laminated sheet conspicuously fixed down by bolts. Barrier remains lowered on the near side. No bargain, payment or passage is already shown.
Source: AP: Rail Workers Gain Sick Leave After Imposed Contract (2023-02)
Source: Union Pacific: Train Types and Hump Yards (undated)
CROSS-01-B · Geographic Contraband
The checkpoint officer spots “Gulf of Mexico” on your map. Trump renamed it. The officer holds the map by one corner, like it might leak Mexicans.
Passage → He lets you pass after folding the offending Gulf out of sight. The ocean has been contained.
Diversion → You take the detour. Both names continue to contain the same water.
Permit receipt → Your permit is accepted. Apparently the map has diplomatic immunity. One Receipt is used.
Permit tag → Your permit is accepted. Apparently the map has diplomatic immunity. Your permit tag remains available.
Bribe success → The payment gets you through. He becomes surprisingly relaxed about where things come from.
Bribe failure → He takes the payment but refuses passage. You have purchased a very patriotic delay.
Refused passage → He refuses passage. You detour around the checkpoint; the Gulf stays where it was.
Scene: Officer holds a folded blank map at arm’s length beside the waiting van. The tiny coastal area, not any human ethnicity, is the visual target.
Source: Gulf renaming
CROSS-01-C · Where Was the Van Born?
The checkpoint officer announces Trump-style extreme vetting. He asks where the van was born. You point to the manufacturer’s plate. “Long-form certificate,” he says.
Passage → You are waved through. The van’s citizenship interview has not improved its suspension.
Diversion → You detour. The van is now accused of taking jobs from American vans.
Permit receipt → Your permit is accepted. The van is apparently a naturalized cargo space. One Receipt is used.
Permit tag → Your permit is accepted. The van is apparently a naturalized cargo space. Your permit tag remains available.
Bribe success → The payment opens the barrier. The van has qualified for the investor route.
Bribe failure → The payment is taken; the barrier stays down. The van’s investment has become foreign aid.
Refused passage → Passage is refused. You take the detour before he asks the spare tire for its grandparents.
Scene: An officer bends toward a blank manufacturer plate while the travelers wait beside the van; a towering stack of blank forms dwarfs the tiny plate.
Source: 2025 entry restrictions and extreme vetting
CROSS-02C-A · The Department of Barrier
The crossing office has copied Trump’s “Department of War” makeover. The new nameplate is enormous. Behind it, two workers are holding up the barrier by hand.
Passage → You cross while the workers hold the barrier. The nameplate offers strong moral support.
Diversion → You take the detour. The new department has secured a decisive victory over traffic.
Permit receipt → The permit clears you. A worker lifts the barrier with his actual defense budget: both arms. One Receipt is used.
Permit tag → The permit clears you. A worker lifts the barrier with his actual defense budget: both arms. Your permit tag remains available.
Bribe success → The payment gets the barrier raised. The department has discovered arms funding.
Bribe failure → The payment disappears into the office. The workers still have only the original two arms each.
Terminal failure → You cannot complete this crossing. The expedition ends beneath a nameplate large enough to hide the problem.
Scene: Two tired crossing workers physically support a raised barrier beside an oversized blank office nameplate; the van remains on the approach.
Source: Department of War naming
CROSS-02C-B · Merit-Based Concrete
The crossing boss boasts that he removed DEI from the inspection checklist. He points to a crack in the concrete. “That’s a diversity of surfaces.”
Passage → You make it across. The concrete remains unpersuaded by the personnel policy.
Diversion → You detour. The boss has successfully excluded your van from the bridge.
Permit receipt → Your permit is accepted. Paperwork has passed a load-bearing test that paperwork really shouldn’t be taking. One Receipt is used.
Permit tag → Your permit is accepted. Paperwork has passed a load-bearing test that paperwork really shouldn’t be taking. Your permit tag remains available.
Bribe success → The payment clears the crossing. Merit has turned out to have a cash option.
Bribe failure → The payment is taken, but passage is refused. You have funded another investigation into the concrete’s pronouns.
Terminal failure → This crossing ends the expedition. The boss’s review recommends less diversity in the complaint form.
Scene: Boss proudly displays a blank inspection sheet beside an obvious concrete crack, with the waiting van safely before the crossing.
Source: Trump anti-DEI actions
CROSS-02C-C · The Slot Works
The crossing supervisor has read about TSA’s $45 identity check, which doesn’t guarantee clearance. He likes the principle. His own counter now has a cash slot and a much smaller slot for objections.
Passage → The barrier rises and you cross. He looks disappointed that a procedure has resulted in transportation.
Diversion → You take the diversion. Your objection would fit the slot if folded into a paper airplane.
Permit receipt → Your permit clears you. He checks both sides for a payment he might have missed. One Receipt is used.
Permit tag → Your permit clears you. He checks both sides for a payment he might have missed. Your permit tag remains available.
Bribe success → Your payment opens the barrier. For once, the useful part of the machine moves.
Bribe failure → He takes your money and keeps the barrier down. The cash slot, he explains, is fully operational.
Terminal failure → The crossing ends your expedition. He points to the working cash slot as evidence that nothing here is broken.

Scene: The van waits on the near side of a crossing barrier. A separate supervisor indicates a broad slot and a comically narrow slit in an otherwise blank counter. Current occupants are considering the situation; no hands offer money or permits.
Editable overlays: “PAYMENTS” — above broad blank slot; “OBJECTIONS” — above narrow blank slot
Source: Travelers Without REAL ID Could Pay $45 Fee for TSA’s ConfirmID Beginning February 1 (2026-02-01)
CROSS-02D-A · The Privacy Camera
Deep End only
The checkpoint’s Flock camera is advertised as protection. A woman ahead asks who protects her when an officer uses it to stalk her. The guard points to a second camera.
Passage → You pass. The second camera is apparently supervising the first camera’s personal growth.
Diversion → You take the diversion. The privacy notice promises to record your concerns, along with your number plate.
Permit receipt → Your permit is accepted. The guard briefly experiences identifying someone without stalking them. One Receipt is used.
Permit tag → Your permit is accepted. The guard briefly experiences identifying someone without stalking them. Your permit tag remains available.
Bribe success → The payment clears the barrier. Privacy remains unavailable, but passage has a price.
Bribe failure → The payment is taken and passage refused. The camera has preserved an excellent record of the customer experience.
Terminal failure → The crossing ends your expedition. The protection camera continues protecting the guard from having to remember anything.
Scene: Waiting van before a checkpoint camera. A separate woman questions a guard who points toward another camera instead of answering. Blank plates and screens; no private location data.
Source: Flock database misuse to stalk women
CROSS-02D-B · Two Documents, One Person
Deep End only
At the checkpoint, a trans traveler’s renewed federal passport conflicts with her state ID. The guard says the computer cannot reconcile them. She suggests looking up from the computer.
Passage → You clear the crossing. The woman ahead remains one person, despite the office’s impressive ability to manufacture two problems.
Diversion → You divert. The guard says the alternate road is less direct, a subject on which he has considerable experience.
Permit receipt → Your permit clears you. The guard accepts that some documents are allowed to agree with their owner. One Receipt is used.
Permit tag → Your permit clears you. The guard accepts that some documents are allowed to agree with their owner. Your permit tag remains available.
Bribe success → The payment opens the barrier. The computer recognizes money with touching flexibility.
Bribe failure → The payment is taken; passage is refused. Money has been recognized. People remain under review.
Terminal failure → The crossing ends your expedition. The computer displays no conflict with that outcome.

Scene: A separate trans traveler holds two blank identity cards with matching portraits while a guard stares at a blank monitor. Current crew and van wait behind; no body inspection or readable personal data.
Source: Federal passport sex-marker policy
CROSS-02D-C · Screened for Needing Treatment
Deep End only
The checkpoint advertises ICE-style medical screening. A diabetic man asks about treatment. The guard points to his intake form. “We’ve already established that you need some.”
Passage → You pass. The clinic’s treatment plan remains a very thorough description of why it needs a treatment plan.
Diversion → You divert. The intake desk describes your departure as reduced demand for services.
Permit receipt → Your permit is accepted. The crossing can process paper considerably faster than it processes people. One Receipt is used.
Permit tag → Your permit is accepted. The crossing can process paper considerably faster than it processes people. Your permit tag remains available.
Bribe success → The payment clears the barrier. The cash receives immediate attention from a specialist.
Bribe failure → The payment is taken without passage. The office has completed its financial intake.
Terminal failure → The crossing ends your expedition. The intake form is complete; the service it describes remains missing.

Scene: A separate adult at a checkpoint clinic gestures toward an unused treatment chair while a guard displays a blank completed intake form. No medical procedure, distress spectacle or new crew passenger.
Source: Detention medical care beyond intake
CROSS-03-A · His Majesty’s Tollbooth
At the final crossing, an official admires Trump’s “LONG LIVE THE KING!” post about trying to kill New York’s congestion toll. He has made himself a paper crown. It catches on the tollbooth ceiling.
Passage → He lifts the barrier and you cross. The crown stays wedged in the ceiling, governing the booth without him.
Diversion → You take the diversion. His Majesty points the way with a plastic coffee stirrer.
Permit receipt → Your permit clears the van. He lowers his crown to inspect a document with more authority. One Receipt is used.
Permit tag → Your permit clears the van. He lowers his crown to inspect a document with more authority. Your permit tag remains available.
Bribe success → Your payment opens the barrier. The royal treasury turns out to be a trouser pocket.
Bribe failure → He takes the payment but refuses passage. The royal treasury is flourishing; the transport policy needs work.
Terminal failure → The crossing ends your expedition. Inside the booth, His Majesty has to remove his crown to reach the kettle.

Scene: Current occupants wait with the van on the near side of the final barrier. A separate crossing official wears a bent paper crown that touches the low booth ceiling; a plastic stirrer and kettle sit inside. No payment or crossing has occurred.
Source: New York governor’s transcript on the federal congestion-pricing reversal attempt (2025-02-19)
Source: Southern District of New York: Congestion-pricing opinion (2026-03-03)
CROSS-03-B · Approved Version of the Journey
The crossing office follows Trump’s demand for a more flattering American history. The officer weighs your case folder. “That’s a lot of country that needs improving.”
Passage → You cross with the case. The country’s flattering biography has acquired an awkward appendix.
Diversion → You detour. The officer starts describing your absence as public satisfaction.
Permit receipt → Your permit clears you. The folder remains inconveniently full. One Receipt is used.
Permit tag → Your permit clears you. The folder remains inconveniently full. Your permit tag remains available.
Bribe success → The payment opens the barrier. Your story has found a sponsor.
Bribe failure → The payment is kept, but passage is refused. Sponsorship does not include editorial control.
Terminal failure → You cannot complete this crossing. The expedition ends; the official version is already shorter.
Scene: Officer weighs a thick, unlettered case folder beside a conspicuously thin blank official-history booklet, with the van waiting behind.
Source: White House history intervention
CROSS-03-C · The Department of Arrivals
The crossing office is copying Trump’s plan to dismantle the Education Department: abolish the desk, announce better service. Your appointment is being held on an upturned bucket.
Passage → You cross. The bucket receives no credit for its public service.
Diversion → You detour. The bucket is now managing both arrivals and complaints.
Permit receipt → Your permit clears you. The bucket has retained institutional knowledge. One Receipt is used.
Permit tag → Your permit clears you. The bucket has retained institutional knowledge. Your permit tag remains available.
Bribe success → The payment gets you through. A private contractor immediately offers to rent you a second bucket.
Bribe failure → The payment is kept, but passage is refused. The contractor bills for bucket access.
Terminal failure → The crossing cannot be completed. The expedition ends; the bucket has been shortlisted for promotion.
Scene: An official balances blank appointment papers on an upturned bucket where a desk used to stand. Keep the van before the barrier.
Source: Education Department dismantling direction
